title: Potions and blows
description: Give the hero actions of their own, and keep the rules for health and potions inside the class.

tasks.title: Give objects things they can do
tasks.body: A method is a function inside a class. def heal(self, amount): with self.health = self.health + amount inside changes that hero's own health. nova.heal(3) calls it, and Python passes nova in as self.
tasks.detail: Methods keep the rules in one place: take_hit() can make sure health never goes below 0, wherever a hit comes from. Each object keeps its own state, so healing Nova leaves Kai alone. A method can also answer a question by returning a value, like is_alive().

tasks.code:
class Hero:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
        self.health = 10

    def take_hit(self, damage):
        self.health = max(0, self.health - damage)

    def is_alive(self):
        return self.health > 0

nova = Hero("Nova")
kai = Hero("Kai")
nova.take_hit(4)
kai.take_hit(15)
print(nova.health, nova.is_alive())
print(kai.health, kai.is_alive())
tasks.note: Both heroes run the same take_hit(), but each changes only its own health. Kai's 15 damage stops at 0, because the rule lives in the method.

tasks.question: Just after nova.take_hit(4), before Kai is hit, what is kai.health?
tasks.why: Nova and Kai are separate objects with their own health. Hitting Nova changes nothing about Kai.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: add a heal(amount) method that never goes above 10, and heal Nova by 7. Then check kai.is_alive() after healing Nova.

Write a class Hero with a name, health that starts at 10, and potions that start at 2, and three methods. hit(damage) takes the damage off the health, never below 0. drink() uses a potion, if there is one left, to add 5 health, never above 10; with no potions it does nothing. status() returns text like Nova 10/10 potions: 2. Then ask for the hero's name and read commands until the command end: hit, followed by the damage on the next line, or drink. After each command, print the hero's status.
tasks.starter: # Define class Hero with hit(), drink() and status()
hints: Each method changes or reads only self's attributes. max() and min() keep the health between 0 and 10.
status() returns the text instead of printing it, and the loop prints it. The loop reads a command, acts on it, prints, and reads the next one, until end.
With other names: def recharge(self): with if self.cells > 0: inside, and self.cells = self.cells - 1 uses up one cell.

error_hints.text: Each attribute must be set in __init__ with self., and each method called through the hero: hero.drink().
Inside a method, reach the hero's attributes through self, such as self.health, never health on its own.
Every method needs self as its first parameter, and hit() needs the damage as well.
The loop asked for another command after end. Check the command before acting on it, and stop at end.
After a hit of 4, Nova has 6/10 and 2 potions. A potion adds 5, but never above 10: 10/10 and 1 potion.
A hit of 12 leaves 0, never less. A potion then brings back 5.
With no potions left, drink() changes nothing, and the status is printed all the same.
Check a longer fight with several hits and drinks.
Check a hero who does nothing at all: no commands, so nothing is printed.

similar_example.note: A method that uses something up only when there is some left. Your hero has three methods, and limits on its health.

other_ways.note: MAX is a class attribute: one value shared by every hero. := reads the next command inside the while line itself.
